sections.title: The "let's" form
sections.content: The imperative isn't only for telling one person what to do — the 1st person plural form ("-junk/-jünk") is how Hungarian says "let's...". együtt ("together") pairs naturally with it, the same way -val/-vel does — együtt Károllyal means "together with Károly".

items.english: Let's cut some onion, then boil some water.

sections.content: főzzünk reuses főz — the same verb behind A1's főzni ("to cook") — now with the -j turned into "zz" the same way vág and forral turn theirs, just applied to a z-final stem instead of a plain consonant.
